## FIX (auto-loop , backend/logic/perf/storage/code-health)  (40)

- [high] **Promo code discount is validated and shown to the customer but NEVER applied to the charge (customer pays full price)** , `app/api/stripe/booking-pay-intent/route.ts:137, 152-156` (bugs)
  - The booking flow collects a promo code (PayConfirmStep.tsx:224 sends promo_code in the POST /api/bookings body) and /api/promo/validate returns {valid:true, discount_amount, new_total} so the UI shows 'you save CHF X'. But: (1) createBookingSchema (lib/validations.ts:34-60) does NOT include promo_code/gift_card_code/total_price, so Zod strips them silently and POST /api/bookings never reads/persists the promo. (2) booking-pay-intent computes priceChf = service.price + extras (line 137) and the charge amount (line 152-156) with NO promo lookup at all; only the Solen-Plus member waiver is applied. The endpoint's own comment (lines 76-78) admits 'promo discounts are not yet applied to the booking Stripe charge'. Net effect: a customer who applies a valid promo code is charged the FULL price while the UI told them they'd save money. Fix: thread promo_code through the booking row (add to schema + persist), re-validate it server-side in booking-pay-intent (re-run the promo_codes lookup + constraint checks), subtract the discount from amountRappen before computing the fee, and increment promo_codes.current_uses on payment_intent.succeeded in the webhook. Gift card code (formData.giftCardCode, PayConfirmStep:225) is dropped the same way.
- [high] **Salon search + PDP ship all 101 salon columns (select *) to anonymous clients, including stripe_account_id, owner_id, search_doc, score_details** , `app/api/salons/route.ts:88` (perf)
  - Both the list endpoint (line 88, .select(`*, services(...)`)) and the PDP endpoint (app/api/salons/[slug]/route.ts:22, .select('*')) return every salon column. I curled /api/salons?category=coiffeur&city=basel&with_slots=1 and counted 101 keys per salon, including stripe_account_id, owner_id, score_details, search_doc (an FTS document that grows), verification_warnings, frozen_reason, rejection_reason, member_commission_waiver_rate. SalonResultCard reads ~15 fields. This is both over-fetch (31KB for 8 results, mostly unused) and a data-exposure problem (owner/payment fields sent to logged-out visitors). Never ship search_doc/score_details/stripe_account_id/owner_id to the client.
- [high] **City+category search runs city lookup, test-salon count, and availability scans as sequential awaits before the main query** , `app/api/salons/route.ts:101` (perf)
  - Measured: ?category=coiffeur alone = 0.24s; +city=basel = 0.5s warm / 3.1s cold; +date = 1.1s. The city branch (line 101) awaits a fetch of ALL cities, THEN a separate count:exact query to decide test-salon hiding (line 120), THEN the main query. Each extra filter (date lines 296/356/370, price 275, gender 242, service 144, period 206, instant 164, open_now 223) adds its own sequential await resolving salon-id sets one after another. Fix: run the independent id-resolving sub-queries (city row lookup, gender, price, service, availability windows) with Promise.all instead of serial awaits, and fold the 'real salons exist?' count into the cities lookup so the city branch is one round-trip, not two.
- [high] **Inspo feed fires 5 extra discovery_feed RPC calls on mount just to get a count + cover per category** , `app/[locale]/inspo/page.tsx:158` (perf)
  - On mount the inspo page does Promise.all over DISCOVERY_CATEGORIES (all/hair/nails/lashes/brows = 5 keys, CategoryTabBar.tsx:13) each calling fetch(`/api/discovery/feed?category=KEY&limit=1`) (line 161-166) purely to read d.total and the top item's cover image. That is 5 full discovery_feed RPC executions (each computes a window count(*) over the discovery table) in addition to the real feed fetch and the chip-terms/category-order/profile fetches firing in the same render. So the inspo page issues ~9 API calls before showing content. Fix: add one /api/discovery/category-meta endpoint that returns {key: {count, cover}} for all categories in a single RPC (GROUP BY category with a representative cover), and replace the per-category fan-out with that single call.
- [high] **Salon PDP is fully client-rendered: SSR ships an empty skeleton, then a useEffect fetch on first paint blocks all content** , `app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonDetailV3.tsx:84` (perf)
  - page.tsx renders SalonDetailV3, a 'use client' component that fetches /api/salons/[slug] in a useEffect (line 84-108) only after the JS bundle hydrates. Until then the user sees LoadingSkeleton. Meanwhile the server already hits the DB for the SAME salon twice in layout.tsx (generateMetadata line 21 selects name/address/cover/rating; the layout default export line 99 selects name/categories) — so the salon row is queried 3x per PDP view (2 server, 1 client) and the actual content waits on a client round-trip (measured 0.9s for the API alone, on top of bundle download + hydrate). Fix: make the PDP a server component that fetches the salon once on the server, passes it to a client child for interactivity, and reuses that fetch result for the metadata (Next dedupes a cached fetch). This removes the duplicate queries and gives real SSR/streaming.
- [high] **instant_bookable & date filters fetch ~17k slot rows to derive ~21 salon IDs** , `app/api/salons/route.ts:164-179, 295-305, 354-386` (storage)
  - The instant_bookable filter runs `availability_slots.select('salon_id').eq('status','available').gte/lte(starts_at, 48h-window)` and then dedupes in JS to a Set. Verified against the live DB: that 48h window matches 16,902 slot rows (EXPLAIN ANALYZE: Actual Rows 16,902, 4,257 shared buffer blocks ~33MB read), and the 14-day window used by the `date`/post-query availability blocks matches 92,961 rows, all to compute only ~21 distinct salon_ids (total slots table = 221,188 rows). PostgREST also caps results (default 1000), so on real data instant_bookable SILENTLY DROPS salons whose slots sort past row 1000 (a correctness bug on top of the waste). The `period` filter already solved this exact problem with the `salons_with_slot_in_hours` RPC (line 206) that does DISTINCT server-side. Fix: add a `salons_with_available_slots(p_from, p_to)` RPC returning `SELECT DISTINCT salon_id` (and reuse it for instant_bookable, the `date` narrow filter at 295, and the post-query availableIds at 354). The existing idx_slots_date_status (status, starts_at) already supports it; the RPC returns ~21 rows instead of ~17k.

- [medium] **reviews/eligibility endpoint throws a PostgREST 22P02 error (subquery used inside an .in() filter) -> always returns ineligible** , `app/api/reviews/eligibility/route.ts:23` (bugs)
  - .not("id","in","(SELECT booking_id FROM reviews WHERE booking_id IS NOT NULL)") is invalid PostgREST: the in operator expects a literal CSV list, not a SQL subquery, so PostgREST tries to cast the words 'SELECT booking_id ...' to uuid. Reproduced live against the REST API: returns {"code":"22P02","message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"SELECT booking_id FROM reviews WHERE booking_id IS NOT NULL\""}. The code destructures only { data: booking } and never checks the error, so booking is null and the route returns {eligible:false} for EVERY user, even ones with a completed un-reviewed booking. Mitigant: no live caller wires to this endpoint today (the actual reviews page at app/[locale]/salon/[slug]/reviews/page.tsx:99-104 and /api/reviews/my-booking:30-37 both use the correct two-step exclusion), so customer impact is currently nil, but the endpoint is broken for any future caller. Fix: copy the my-booking pattern (fetch completed booking ids, fetch reviewed booking_ids, exclude in JS) or use .not("id","in",`(${ids.join(",")})`) with a resolved id list.

Fix: seed/derive realistic suitable_gender per service (e.g. from category/name) so the filter actually partitions salons, or hide the control until the data supports it.

- [medium] **Express-rebook suggested date/time is computed in the SERVER timezone, not Europe/Zurich** , `app/api/bookings/express-rebook/route.ts:82-88` (bugs)

- [medium] **profile/live-state queries phantom columns, silently disabling the 'upcoming' state** , `app/api/profile/live-state/route.ts:53` (storage)
  - The upcoming-booking query selects `services(name), salons(slug, name, neighborhood)`. Verified against the live DB: `salons.neighborhood` does NOT exist (salons has `quartier`/`postal_code`) and `services.name` does NOT exist (services has name_de/name_en). PostgREST errors on a non-existent column in an embedded select; the route wraps each priority in try/catch and falls through to the NEXT state, so the highest-priority 'appointment within 24h' card never renders even when a booking exists. This endpoint is polled every 60s by every visitor on /profile (ProfilePage.tsx:792). Fix: change to `services(name_de, name_en)` and drop `neighborhood` (use `quartier`). Net effect: fixes a dead feature AND stops a guaranteed-failing query firing every 60s per user.
- [low] **unavailable-dates derives calendar days from slot instants in UTC while time-slots uses Zurich day-boundaries (date mismatch for late slots)** , `app/api/availability/unavailable-dates/route.ts:59-63` (bugs)
  - availableDates is built with new Date(slot.starts_at).toISOString().split('T')[0] (UTC calendar day), but /api/availability/time-slots/route.ts:34-41 explicitly computes Swiss-local day boundaries for the same slots, and the codebase notes slots store true instants. A slot whose Zurich-local day differs from its UTC day (any slot at/after 22:00 Zurich in summer = 20:00 UTC, crossing into the next... actually >=00:00 UTC) would be attributed to the wrong calendar date here, greying out an available day or vice versa in the booking calendar. Latent: current live slots top out at 17:45 UTC (19:45 Zurich), so no slot crosses UTC midnight and the bug doesn't manifest with today's data; it surfaces if any salon adds late-evening hours. Fix: derive the day with the same Europe/Zurich formatting the time-slots route uses, so both calendar surfaces agree.

- [low] **Salon prices bypass formatPrice/formatCurrency, built as raw `CHF ${n}` strings** , `app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonServicesSheet.tsx:282` (codehealth)
  - SalonServicesSheet.tsx renders prices as `CHF {s.price}` (L282, L455) and totals as `CHF ${total}` (L340, L478); components-legacy/booking/PayConfirmStep.tsx does the same. lib/format.ts already exports formatPrice(amount, locale) and lib/format-currency.ts formatCurrency, which apply Swiss grouping/decimals and locale. The raw template strings skip thousands separators and locale, so a 1200 CHF package renders 'CHF 1200' not 'CHF 1’200'. Fix: replace the inline `CHF ${...}` with formatPrice() in these salon/booking price slots for consistency with the rest of the app (CardText/PriceFrom already use it).
- [low] **PayConfirmStep leans on `as any` casts for translations and salon fields** , `components-legacy/booking/PayConfirmStep.tsx:54` (codehealth)

This disables type checking on a payment-critical screen (a renamed field silently becomes undefined, e.g. cancellationHours falls back to 24). Fix: type the salon prop with the real fields (extend the Salon type to include cancellation_window_hours/average_rating/review_count) and drop the `as any` on useTranslations (next-intl is typed); remove the casts so a schema change surfaces at compile time.

A failed save is silently lost (the 'saved' set never updates and the user gets no feedback). Note: PhotoGallery is currently reached only via ChatWindow, and chat messaging is OFF, so impact is latent. Fix: add `catch (err) { console.error('[PhotoGallery] nail-inspo save failed:', err); }` (and ideally surface a toast) so it's correct when/if the surface is revived.
- [low] **Search page refetches the user's favorites (and joined salon rows) on every mount, independent of the result fetch** , `app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx:700` (perf)

Fix: add a lightweight /api/profile/favorites?ids_only=1 mode that returns just salon_id from the favorites table (skip the salons join entirely) for the heart-state use case, and cache it (it rarely changes within a session).
- [low] **Edge-runtime customer routes call getSession() which does a network token-refresh round-trip per request** , `app/api/salons/[slug]/route.ts:14` (perf)
  - Several read-mostly customer endpoints call supabase.auth.getSession() at the top of every GET to derive an optional user (PDP route line 14, discovery feed line 20, bookings/user, favorites). On the supabase-ssr server client getSession validates/refreshes the auth cookie, adding latency to requests that, for anonymous traffic, do not need a user at all (the PDP only uses user.id to allow owners to preview inactive salons). Fix: skip the auth call on the anonymous fast path (only call it when the salon is inactive / when personalization is actually requested), or use getUser() guarded behind a cookie-presence check so logged-out visitors pay nothing.
- [low] **SalonVenuesNearby fires a per-PDP /api/salons/by-category fetch from the client after the main salon load** , `app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonVenuesNearby.tsx:48` (perf)

This is a third serial network hop before the below-the-fold rail appears. Fix: defer it with an IntersectionObserver so it only fires when the rail scrolls near the viewport (it is far below the fold), and/or include a small nearby-salons slice in the main /api/salons/[slug] response so no second request is needed.
- [low] **live-state runs up to 6 sequential round-trips on a 60s poll** , `app/api/profile/live-state/route.ts:49-200` (storage)
  - The priority resolver runs as many as 6 sequential awaited Supabase queries (upcoming booking, loyalty cards+stamps, favorites then off_peak_deals, review replies, past bookings) before returning. The code comment even flags it as a v1 with 'correctness > optimization'. It is polled every 60s while /profile is visible, per logged-in user. For a cold user (no upcoming/loyalty/deal/reply) all 6 fire every minute. Fix: the first three priorities (upcoming, loyalty, deal-source favorites) have no data dependency on each other and can run via Promise.all, then short-circuit on the highest-priority hit; or fold the whole resolver into one SQL function with CTEs as the comment anticipates. Lower severity than the slot scans because per-query row counts are tiny, but it is a recurring fixed-interval cost.
- [low] **PDP reviews sub-page loads ALL reviews unbounded with 3 joins each** , `app/[locale]/salon/[slug]/reviews/page.tsx:71-90` (storage)
  - The /salon/[slug]/reviews page selects every review for the salon (no .limit/.range) with embedded profiles + review_photos + review_replies for each row, ordered by created_at. The header comment acknowledges 'Future v2: infinite-scroll if review count > 50' but ships the full load today. A dedicated paginated endpoint already exists (app/api/reviews/salon/[salon_id]/route.ts paginates at limit 20). Fix: render the first page server-side with `.range(0, 19)` and let SalonReviews page further via the existing /api/reviews/salon endpoint, instead of materializing the entire review history (with three joined child tables) on first paint. Also note the salon row is fetched twice on this page (generateMetadata line 31 + body line 52) — collapse via a cached getter.
- [low] **with_slots path fetches up to 3000 slot rows then keeps 3 per service in JS** , `app/api/salons/route.ts:412-430` (storage)
  - For the search/category card (`?with_slots=1`), after picking the top 3 services per salon the route queries availability_slots `.in('service_id', serviceIds).gte/lte(starts_at, 14d).order(starts_at).limit(3000)` and then, in JS, keeps only the first 3 slots per service (line 429 `if (slotsByService[svcId].length < 3)`). It pulls up to 3000 rows to retain at most 3*serviceCount. On a full results page (20 salons * 3 services = 60 service_ids) over a 14-day window this transfers far more than the ~180 timestamps actually shown. Fix: a lateral/window RPC (`row_number() over (partition by service_id order by starts_at) <= 3`) returns exactly 3 per service server-side. The idx_availability_slots_service_id index (confirmed present in live DB) supports it. Lower severity than instant_bookable because the limit caps the blast radius, but the 3000-row ceiling is still ~16x the rows rendered.
- [low] **Each search results page makes a separate walk-in availability call for every salon** , `app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx:681-701` (storage)
  - After loading a results page, SearchTemplate fires a second request `/api/walkin/availability?salon_ids=<all ids>` to annotate 'Frei in ~X Min' for cards. The underlying getWalkinAvailability is well-batched (fixed query count), but this runs unconditionally for every search page even when zero results are walk-in-enabled, and re-fires on every filter change / pagination. With only ~23 total salons most are not walkin_enabled (getWalkinAvailability early-returns {} after the salons+walkin_enabled lookup). Fix: skip the walk-in call entirely when the active filter set is not walk-in-relevant, or gate it behind the salons already known to have walkin_enabled in the just-returned page payload (the /api/salons response could carry a boolean walkin_enabled so the client avoids the extra round-trip for non-walk-in result sets).
